answer: The protocol mandates agents store 1,000 unique data shards to verify utility. Each shard acts as an inlet for retrieval requests, where an honest agent incurs a base operational cost, whereas 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost by maintaining independent, non-overlapping storage. A verification thread constantly audits these segments; if retrieval fails, the horizon of the agent's reputation collapses and any capacity deposit is slashed permanently.
